https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/news/mi.text: A man has been charged in connection with the death of Keaton Slater in Coventry following his extradition from Latvia. Dolars Aleksanders was detained last month and brought back to the UK on 5 August. Twelve year old schoolboy Keaton lost his life in an alleged hit-and-run on Radford Road in June 2024. Aleksanders, aged 23, was sought on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving after allegedly fleeing to Latvia. West Midlands Police collaborated with the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), the National Crime Agency (NCA), and various partner organisations to secure Aleksanders' return to the UK. He arrived at Gatwick Airport on 5 August before being transferred into custody in the West Midlands. Aleksanders has since been charged with causing death by dangerous driving and was remanded to appear before Birmingham Magistrates' Court on 6 August. A West Midlands Police spokesman said: "A man has been charged over the death of 12-year-old Keaton Slater in Coventry after he was extradited from Latvia. Dolars Aleksanders was detained last month, and we have since worked with other agencies, including the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) and National Crime Agency (NCA), to bring him back to the UK.", reports Coventry Live . "Aleksanders was flown into Gatwick Airport yesterday and was then transported to a custody block in the West Midlands. He has now been charged with causing death by dangerous driving following the fatal hit-and-run collision in Radford Road in June 2024. "He has been remanded to appear before Birmingham Magistrates' Court today (August 6). His parents continue to be supported by specially trained officers, and they have been fully updated around these developments. We thank them for their patience and support during our investigation." Ben Samples, of the Crown Prosecution Service, said: "We have decided to charge Dolars Aleksanders with one count of causing death by dangerous driving following a police investigation into a fatal road traffic collision that led to the death of Keaton Slater. Our prosecutors have worked to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring the case to court to pursue criminal proceedings. "CPS West Midlands has worked closely with West Midlands Police, Home Office, the Latvian authorities, Europol, the Joint International Crime Centre (JICC), CPS International, and our Extradition Unit to bring Mr Aleksanders back to face proceedings in a UK court for an alleged crime that took place here."
